edition: snowmoon.party: an independent edition of Vitalik Buterin's Snowmoon, not affiliated with or endorsed by the author. Rules marked invented were made up for this edition.
name: Minpentai Play, solo against the computer, v1

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: The board is 15 x 10 squares.

book.says: The field has corners (and so edges).

rules.edition: What a glider does at the edge.
rules.text: The board has edges and corners. A glider that would leave the board turns back on that side instead, and stays put for that step.

rules.edition: The whole rule. (Each player starting in a corner is in the book, c4-b94; these starts are not in corners.)
rules.text: Each side starts with 2 towers (Cyan at (1, 2) and (1, 7), Amber at (13, 2) and (13, 7)) and there are six rocks, all mirrored.

book.says: Each player has a symbol; a copy of it anywhere on the board lets them see around it.

rules.edition: Symbols are drawn as towers, one square each; they are also the score.
rules.text: A tower is your score, your sight, and where you may place.

book.says: Gliders exist and fly across the field.

rules.edition: One square a step, in a straight line, four directions (eight under "diag"), never stopping on its own.
rules.text: A glider moves one square a step in a straight line, up, down, left or right (diagonally too only under the "diag" rule), and never stops on its own.

book.says: Walls can reflect gliders, and a wall can be destroyed.

rules.edition: Walls are single squares; two hits to break; the first hit reflects; any side's glider cracks any square.
rules.text: A square blocks a glider: the first hit cracks it and turns the glider straight back; the second breaks the square and the glider. Any glider cracks any square, its own side's too.

book.says: There are rocks on the field.

rules.edition: Rocks are fixed, bounce every glider straight back, never break, and never make gliders (in the book, gliders hitting rocks make more gliders, c4-b108; not here).
rules.text: A rock is fixed, turns every glider straight back, and never breaks.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: Every glider moves at the same moment.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: Two gliders of different sides break each other if they head for the same square, swap squares, or cross. A side's own gliders pass through each other.

rules.edition: The whole rule. (In the book a stray glider can wreck its own side, c4-b109; left out here.)
rules.text: A glider reaching an opponent's tower destroys it and breaks. Your own tower turns it straight back.

rules.edition: The whole rule. (The book's boards fill with debris, c4-b140.)
rules.text: Broken pieces leave nothing behind.

book.says: Play begins with an initiation phase in which players put down squares, then runs on its own, with intervention turns from time to time.

rules.edition: A setup turn at step 0 and one every 12 steps (in the book the first comes after about a thousand turns).
rules.text: A setup turn at step 0, then a turn to act every 12 steps; between turns the match runs on its own.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: 8 points a turn: glider 4, square 1, tower 4. Unspent points are lost.

book.says: In an intervention turn, players put down more squares near any copy of their symbols.

rules.edition: Within 3 squares counting diagonals, of towers held when the turn began; gliders, squares or towers.
rules.text: Place on any empty square within 3 squares, counting diagonals, of a tower you had when the turn began.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: Both sides place at the same time without seeing each other's choices; two pieces placed on one square cancel each other.

book.says: A copy of your symbol lets you see everything within thirty squares; the field starts dark.

rules.edition: 3 squares, not thirty (2 under "sight2").
rules.text: You see every square within 3 of one of your towers; the rest is dark.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: Rocks are shown everywhere; an opponent's tower you cannot see is shown where you last saw it.

book.says: A player whose symbols have all been eliminated is out.

rules.edition: With two players, out means lost; both at once is a draw.
rules.text: A side with no towers left loses; both at the same step is a draw.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: At step 96 the match stops: most towers wins, equal is a draw.

rules.edition: Resigning counts as a loss.
rules.text: You may resign; it counts as a loss.

book.says: Every game has some kind of new rule.

rules.edition: One of four rules, drawn from the seed; the four rules are invented.
rules.text: One of four new rules is drawn from the seed at the start of every match, and both players see it.

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: The computer players see only what their towers light (Play's; Learn's practice bot is not part of this ruleset).

rules.edition: The whole rule.
rules.text: A match's seed is a whole number from 0 to 999,999. Its first random number draws the new rule; the computer player takes the rest, in order.
